cohort: 131 pregnant women with sickle cell disease (SCD) and 1310 pregnant women without SCD
finding: Infants born to mothers with SCD were more likely to be small for gestational age, preterm, require NNU admission, and their mothers were at higher risk of pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, induction of labour, and caesarean birth.
mod_finding: The risk of adverse outcomes was highest in haemoglobin SS (HbSS) pregnancies, with no strong evidence that haemoglobin SC (HbSC) pregnancies were at higher risk of preterm birth, caesarean delivery, or NNU admission, though pre-eclampsia/eclampsia was more frequent in HbSC pregnancies.
